channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: The practice of burning wood for charcoal is depleting forests and harming the environment, according to the Environmental Protection Agency.

item.title: Civil society group demands Sierra Leone finance minister's sacking
item.description: The CSOs Consortium on Public Accountability wants Finance Minister Sheku Ahmed Fantamadi Bangura removed immediately, a call a Politico SL guest writer says is misplaced.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents have never won the presidency
item.description: An analyst says the office has repeatedly served as a political dead end, and asks whether the current Vice President's path is already closed.

item.title: Mali and Türkiye discuss resuming Turkish Airlines flights to Bamako
item.description: Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga raised the restart of Turkish Airlines flights to Bamako with Turkish Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz in Antalya on Tuesday.

item.title: Somaliland Ports Authority rejects Djibouti training claim
item.description: The Somaliland Ports Authority demanded a public correction from Djibouti's authority over staff training allegations.

item.title: ZB Financial Holdings profit after tax falls 31% despite balance sheet growth
item.description: The Zimbabwean financial services group's core earnings rose sharply even as its headline profit fell, according to figures reported this week.

item.title: El Niño rains threaten Tanzania's vulnerable populations
item.description: Children, pregnant women, the elderly, and disabled face heightened risks as heavy rains are forecast until January.

item.title: Mozambique government backs Temane power plant with World Bank funds
item.description: Cabinet approves a support package including US$65 million from the World Bank to finish the gas-fired plant.

item.title: France and EU back Mauritius with Rs 6.3 billion for water crisis
item.description: The package combines a 100 million euro AFD loan with a 20 million euro EU grant, pending final AFD board approval.

item.title: Cameroon minister Hamadou Moustapha dies at 81
item.description: The minister in charge of mission at the presidency died after a long illness at his home in Yaounde.

item.title: Sierra Leone teachers face discipline for census training
item.description: The Teaching Service Commission warns educators abandoning classrooms for census work will face action.

item.title: Tanzania balances coastal development with environment
item.description: The Mwalimu Julius Nyerere Bridge connects Kigamboni and Dar es Salaam, supporting economic growth.

item.title: Women achieve historic representation in Sao Tome and Principe parliament
item.description: 18 women now sit in the 55-seat National Assembly, the highest number ever.

item.title: São Tomé and Príncipe launches Resilands climate resilience initiative
item.description: The Green Climate Fund-financed project will fund early warning systems and disaster risk management, with the UN Economic Commission for Africa carrying out the work.

item.title: Ghana launches $18.8m rice project to aid 20,000 northern farmers
item.description: The African Development Bank grant funds seven districts across four northern regions, targeting more than 20,000 smallholder rice farmers.

item.title: Eswatini farmers test new methods to grow more food
item.description: Farmers in Shiselweni demonstrated techniques to improve production and protect crops and livestock as weather patterns change.

item.title: UNIMA students protest power cuts
item.description: Students say ongoing blackouts are hindering exam preparation and causing security fears.

item.title: Algeria coach skips Eswatini media briefing before CAF qualifier
item.description: Rafik Saïfi was at the stadium for training but did not meet reporters, and CAF rules set a USD 5 000 fine for a first offence.

item.title: Malian man dies after falling from Malabo Gendarmerie window
item.description: Mamadu Maiga, detained in the Bettomax betting probe, died after a fall from a window in the National Gendarmerie in Malabo on Saturday night.

item.title: South Sudan joins global telecom talks in Qatar
item.description: The nation aims to shape international ICT policy and boost digital development.

item.title: 600 pupils in Ashaiman taught about drugs and cybercrime
item.description: Officials from three agencies gave basic school pupils in Ashaiman, Greater Accra, warnings on substance abuse and online harm.

item.title: US warns Liberia on investment climate
item.description: American firms face corruption, delays, and demands for bribes, says State Department report.

item.title: Algeria's weather office warns of gusts over 80 km/h in seven provinces
item.description: Violent winds are forecast to begin at 9 a.m. Wednesday and continue until 3 a.m. Thursday across several provinces.

item.title: BTK Bank and Tecnocasa Tunisie partner for property access
item.description: The agreement aims to simplify the property buying process for individuals, investors, and Tunisians abroad.

item.title: Nigerian-born Emehelu becomes New Jersey's first immigrant lieutenant governor
item.description: Shirley Emehelu, who emigrated from Nigeria as a child, was sworn in on Monday and also took on the role of Secretary of State.

item.title: Uganda signs deal to host African Union humanitarian agency
item.description: The Host Country Agreement was signed at State House, Entebbe, and the agency is expected to be fully operational within three years.

item.title: Cameroon lawmakers seek release of CFAF 5,000 billion in financing
item.description: National Assembly Speaker Théodore Datouo opened the budget session by urging faster delivery of stalled development projects.

item.title: Second convicted murderer dies in Naïcha case
item.description: Fahami Moustoifa, sentenced to death, died after being admitted to El Maarouf hospital.

item.title: Cameroon regulator flags CFAF18.6 billion in telecom violations
item.description: ART identified 93 violations involving CAMTEL, Orange Cameroon and MTN Cameroon, with the state-owned CAMTEL accounting for the largest share.

item.title: Liberia retires 2,718 civil servants
item.description: The government aims to improve pension administration and ensure timely benefit payments.

item.title: Edo Governor vows to sign death warrants for kidnappers
item.description: Governor Monday Okpebholo stated he would sign execution orders for convicted kidnappers, even if they were family.

item.title: Tunis hosts 27th Theatre Days from November 21
item.description: 12 productions from 11 Arab and African countries will compete for the Golden Tanit award.

item.title: Botswana graduates face job scarcity due to slow business growth
item.description: The nation's economy struggles to absorb educated youth as businesses lack expansion and innovation.

item.title: ArcelorMittal Liberia steps up railway safety drive in Grand Bassa
item.description: The company and police met Compound #3 residents to warn that trains cannot stop quickly, so people must stay off the tracks.

item.title: Cameroon ships first 17 tons of coffee to China duty-free
item.description: The Ministry of Finance says the shipment qualifies under Beijing's zero-tariff policy, which gives Cameroonian exporters duty-free entry to the Chinese market.

item.title: Wagner and Chinese firms control 40% of CAR forests
item.description: A new report details lost revenue and violations of forestry law due to foreign control of concessions.

item.title: Port-Louis drivers face delays of up to 90 minutes after road closure and crash
item.description: Rue Monseigneur Leen will stay shut until December 21 while crews rebuild a road surface damaged by a landslide.

item.title: Liberian war rights office protests exclusion from memorial unveiling
item.description: The OWECC-L says war victims, survivors and people with disabilities were left out of the November 6 ceremony at the Executive Mansion.

item.title: Police spymaster Busang Lesola reportedly bids to lead Botswana's DIS
item.description: Deputy Commissioner Busang Lesola, who runs Crime Intelligence, is reportedly among those considered to succeed Peter Magosi at the Directorate of Intelligence and Security.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea asks UNESCO prize winners to aid universities
item.description: The government wants laureates to share expertise to strengthen national research and innovation.

item.title: Bor police release brothers who killed sister over marriage
item.description: Two men accused of beating their teenage sister to death for rejecting an arranged marriage have been freed without charges.

item.title: Lofa to host Liberia's third National Agriculture Fair
item.description: The December 10-12 event in Voinjama will bring farmers and agribusinesses from every county together to boost local food output.

item.title: Eswatini minister says local banks hold E21 billion in government bonds
item.description: Finance Minister Neal Rijkenberg says the E1.6 billion Standard Bank loan is part of a wider borrowing mix, not a sign of local refusals.

item.title: Malawi government to appeal K300bn Finance Bank award
item.description: Attorney General Frank Mbeta calls the compensation to the defunct bank excessive and plans a Supreme Court review this week.

item.title: Madagascar plans constitutional referendum
item.description: Officials propose changes to voter registration, campaign rules, and diaspora participation.

item.title: Namibia state firms owe N$11.12 billion
item.description: Taxpayers are exposed to a further N$11.8 billion in state-guaranteed debt, straining the national budget.

item.title: Senate committee adopts Sh71.1bn county fund report
item.description: The Finance and Budget Committee flagged errors in disbursement schedules for additional county funds.

item.title: BCI hosts Christmas games at children's centre
item.description: The bank's Solidarity Christmas initiative included a draughts championship and gift distribution.

item.title: Libya authorizes two PhD programs at University of Benghazi
item.description: The Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research has cleared the university to offer doctoral studies in two education fields.

item.title: Senators question Kasarani Stadium readiness for AFCON 2027
item.description: The Senate Committee on Labour and Social Welfare inspected the Nairobi stadium and questioned its accessibility and emergency preparedness ahead of the December 31 deadline.

item.title: US Democrats' Congress takeover puts Namibia's minerals and AGOA in focus
item.description: Democratic control of both US chambers could reshape Washington's trade and investment priorities toward Africa, including Namibia's mineral wealth.

item.title: Malawi arrests ex-MP Chilapondwa over K884m unpaid VAT
item.description: Revenue authority says the former Ntchisi South MP collected VAT on government electrification contracts without being registered to do so.

item.title: Court rejects State bid to block Mundubile and Zulu bail hearing
item.description: The Lusaka High Court ruled the bail application of opposition leaders Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu and 16 others must now be heard on its merits.

item.title: Burundi Senate president targets police officers
item.description: Gitega: Senate President Gervais Ndirakobuca criticizes judicial police officers for overstepping their legal authority.

item.title: Mahama unveils $10bn 'New Economy' plan for Ghana
item.description: The four-year programme from 2027 to 2030 aims to grow what Ghana produces and processes at home, and will feature in the 2027 Budget.

item.title: ARED brings local authorities and civil society together to prevent conflict in Mandoul
item.description: The meeting in Koumra on November 10, 2026, gathered administrative and military officials with civil society groups to discuss how to keep community tensions from turning.

item.title: Bank of Uganda keeps key rate at 12 per cent as inflation rises
item.description: The central bank held its benchmark rate after an October increase, warning that a weaker shilling and fuel costs could push prices higher still.

item.title: Senate donates N100m to U-17 women's football team
item.description: The Nigerian Senate recognised the Flamingos' World Cup triumph with a significant financial reward.

item.title: Malawi hauliers ground trucks over fuel transport dispute
item.description: Local transporters protest the return of a court-outlawed Delivery Duty Unpaid system favouring foreign firms.

item.title: FAZ clarifies U-15 World Cup winning allowances
item.description: The Football Association of Zambia explained payment details for the U-15 team's victory in Baku, Azerbaijan.

item.title: Zambia: 1,558 teachers idle as rural schools lack staff
item.description: Copperbelt Province Minister Emmanuel Kasambo revealed that 1,247 teachers in Kitwe alone are not assigned to classes.

item.title: Ghana cannot celebrate austerity amid infrastructure deficit, says Bokpin
item.description: Economics Professor Godfred Alufar Bokpin says spending cuts will take a while to reach ordinary Ghanaians, ahead of the 2027 Budget presentation.

item.title: Madagascar's rugby sevens team wins first Olympic medal at Dakar Youth Games
item.description: The Ladies Makis 7's took bronze after beating the Czech Republic 26-10, the country's first Olympic medal since it began competing in 1964.

item.title: Madagascar and Russia advance diploma recognition
item.description: A memorandum of cooperation on higher education and scientific research was signed between the two nations.

item.title: Madagascar's pétanque team targets a double in Thailand
item.description: The four-player squad, led by coach Herinirina Edmond Ratsimba, flies out on November 18 for the 52nd World Championships in Khon Kaen.

item.title: Tshisekedi promulgates law setting conditions for referendum
item.description: President Félix Tshisekedi signed law n° 26/045 on November 9, setting the rules for a referendum in DR Congo.

item.title: Eswatini leaves 56 per cent of capital budget unspent at mid-year
item.description: Government spent E3.4 billion of its E7.8 billion capital allocation by the end of September, with project execution at 44 per cent.

item.title: Eswatini actor Luyanda Mali nominated for UK Handprint award
item.description: Mali, who grew up in Mpaka, also earned three nominations at Ghana's Great Excellence Movie Awards 2026 this year.

item.title: Vinícius Jr sends video message to Sudanese boy who lost both legs
item.description: The Real Madrid winger spoke to 13-year-old Zaher in Arabic, a boy who lost both legs in a drone strike.

item.title: Transitaire inculpé dans l'affaire de faux billets de Reug Reug
item.description: Sidy Ndaw a été inculpé après que le marabout Diéguane Faye l'a accusé de lui avoir remis de faux billets, des accusations qu'il conteste.

item.title: CTG shows over 100 journalists the Morébaya port for Simandou
item.description: Media and content creators toured the port's rail link, berths and worker facilities on Monday, November 9, 2026.

item.title: Parliament restores Afenyo-Markin to ECOWAS delegation
item.description: A dispute over Ghana's representation to the regional parliament ends with the approval of a revised list of nominees.

item.title: Niger hosts CAF mission for 2032 Africa Cup of Nations bid
item.description: A CAF expert visited Niamey from November 8-9 to assess Niger's readiness for the 2032 tournament.

item.title: Benin builds 160-hectare wholesale market at Akassato for 2027 opening
item.description: The Akassato facility, north of Cotonou, will hold food products, warehouses and cold storage, with French market expertise guiding its design.

item.title: Eritrean writer Saleh G. Johar launches English channel on America
item.description: Johar will share reflections on the United States, where he has lived permanently since 2000, as Awate.com marks 26 years.

item.title: Mauritania's national dialogue debates restoring the Senate
item.description: Participants are weighing whether to bring back the upper house that Mohamed Ould Abdel Aziz abolished after it refused to back his plans.

item.title: Morocco's IRESEN discusses smart grids at COP31
item.description: Morocco's Research Institute for Solar Energy and New Energies (IRESEN) highlighted challenges in adapting power grids for renewable energy at COP31 in Antalya.

item.title: N'Djamena university students announce four-day strike over buses and restaurants
item.description: The National Union of Chadian Students says the strike runs from November 10 to 13, 2026, over unmet demands at the University of N'Djamena.

item.title: Tunisia receives 61 million euro donation from Netherlands
item.description: The funds will support the fourth and fifth phases of a coastal protection program.

item.title: Burkina Faso stakeholders seek recognition for biopesticides
item.description: A two-day national workshop in Koudougou on November 10 and 11, 2026, will draft a multi-stakeholder roadmap on approving biopesticides.

item.title: Burkina Faso hosts 4th Sino-Burkinabè Film Week
item.description: Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso will screen 14 films from November 12-15, 2026.

item.title: Guinea court jails eight foreign gold miners and frees one man
item.description: The Dixinn court in Conakry sentenced eight Togolese and Burkinabe men to two years in prison and banned all nine from Guinean territory for five years.

item.title: Mauritania announces start of Jumada al-Ula on Wednesday
item.description: The National Moon Sighting Committee said Wednesday, November 11, 2026, is the first day of the Islamic month of Jumada al-Ula, year 1448.

item.title: Sierra Leone presents Mental Health Bill 2026 to Parliament committee
item.description: The Health Ministry seeks to replace the 1902 Lunacy Act with a modern legal framework for mental healthcare.

item.title: 470 women screened in Koper for cancers
item.description: A mobile clinic offered breast self-examination training, mammograms, and cervical cancer screenings.

item.title: Uganda's Tayebwa presses EU for climate finance without more debt
item.description: The Deputy Speaker, who leads the OACPS Parliamentary Assembly, wants climate aid for vulnerable states to stop adding to their debt burdens.

item.title: Algeria inspects Moroccan toxic water pollution
item.description: Ministers visited Tlemcen to assess environmental damage from untreated industrial and wastewater discharges.

item.title: Tanzania to host 2027 East Africa Jua Kali trade fair
item.description: The nation officially accepted the responsibility for organizing the 27th East African Community Small and Medium Traders Exhibition.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea attends TRT World Forum in Turkey
item.description: Minister Juan José Ekuna Esono Mangué led the nation's delegation at the Istanbul event discussing global challenges.

item.title: Mali Council donates food to Guinean returnees
item.description: Five tonnes of rice and other supplies will aid young Malian returnees.

item.title: Fire destroys dozens of homes and part of a market in Chad village
item.description: Witnesses say strong winds carried flames from one compound to the next in Koubo Azarack, Salamat province, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026.

item.title: Angola president barred from third term
item.description: President João Lourenço cannot seek re-election in 2027 due to constitutional term limits.

item.title: Senegal reports 649 food poisoning cases in Kébémer
item.description: No new cases of acute digestive syndrome have been reported in the last 24 hours.

item.title: Guinea and France honour veterans on Armistice Day in Conakry
item.description: Conakry ceremonies marked the 108th anniversary of the 1918 Armistice, with a 100 million Guinean franc aid package for needy veterans.

item.title: Niger president meets Sahel education ministers
item.description: Ministers from Burkina Faso and Mali discussed implementing the Alliance of Sahel States' education roadmap.

item.title: Luanda faces prolonged fuel shortage
item.description: Motorists in Angola's capital are struggling to find gasoline, leading to long queues and traffic disruptions.

item.title: Tunisia drafts specifications to regulate motorcycle sales
item.description: The Commerce Ministry wants sales structured around professional networks, with about two million motorcycles on the roads but only 20,000 registered.

item.title: Djibouti revises labour code with social partners
item.description: Minister Yonis Ali Guedi opened talks on November 8 to update labour laws for modern employment realities.

item.title: South Africa's unemployment rate rises to 33.7%
item.description: Graduates still have a better chance of finding work, with an 11.9% unemployment rate in the third quarter of 2026.

item.title: 13 airport authority staff charged over neglect and wire theft
item.description: Court papers list far narrower charges than the minister's claims of terrorism and a Shs23 billion repair bill at Entebbe airport.
